header: The Pure AI Assistant Engine for DSP Intranet. My aim here is to get rid of regex language parsing and stopword patchwork completely. Architecture:

1. I leave 100% of Natural Language Understanding to the LLM (Groq LLaMA 3.3 70B / gpt-oss-120b): it understands any human phrasing, pronouns ("I", "we"), synonyms, typos, and extracts clean parameters.
2. My code does 100% of Data Access: it executes pure deterministic queries against data tables (hospital, employee SQL, circular embeddings, holidays, PAX).

symbols.name: ID_LIKE
doc: I never send a ticket, a P.No or a phone number in the question to a third party just to be routed; the employee engine handles these.

symbols.name: CHATTY_LINE
doc: A line that really is small talk or a question about the assistant itself. I believe the model's word "conversational" ONLY for such a line: a line about a notice, a rule or a fact ("OTP valid for five minutes") that the model misreads as chatter must go on to the search, which answers it from the documents ("a wrong guess must never replace a right answer").

symbols.name: parseQueryWithLlm
symbols.sig: export async function parseQueryWithLlm( query: string, opts: { llm?: (system: string, user: string) => Promise<string> } = {},): Promise<ToolCall | null>
doc: Natural-language understanding by the language model (Gemini). Returns null when it cannot give a VALID answer (no key, timeout, bad JSON, unknown tool): the caller then continues with the original pipeline, which has its own tested understanding. I never let it guess a tool from keywords: an earlier keyword fallback sent "MD approval for gate pass" to the hospital doctor list and "what is dr reddys policy" to a doctor schedule. `opts.llm` lets a test supply the model's raw JSON text.

symbols.name: NAME_STOP
doc: I list here the words that are never part of a doctor's name (pronouns, filler, the title, time and token words).

symbols.name: nameTokens
doc: Returns the name words a person typed, lower-case, without filler; [] means no usable name was given.

symbols.name: findDoctors
doc: Doctors whose name matches EVERY typed word as a whole name part (a word of 4+ letters may be the start of a part: "rajeev" = "rajeev", "karma" = "karmakar"; a short word must be exact). I do no substring matching: "rohit" must not find "Sarohit". Current doctors win over retired/transferred ones when both match.
